```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r include=FALSE}
require(tidyverse)
require(tigerstats)
davisdata <- read.csv(file="UCDavis.csv")
```
## Our Goal is to answer this question Is there a difference between the alcohol consumed between the row
## you choose to sit in??

## Now with ggplot - first select the basic data

```{r}
basicCN <- ggplot(davisdata,aes(y=alcohol,x=Seat))
```
## Now add in boxplot

```{r}
basicCN + geom_boxplot()
```
  
  
### get fancy  

```{r}
basicCN + geom_boxplot(notch=TRUE,outlier.color = "red") + stat_boxplot(geom ='errorbar') + labs(title="Fancy notch boxplot \n with 2 lines")
```

The students in the back tend to drink more alcohol rather than the students in the front.

## Numerical Summaries

```{r}
favstats(alcohol~Seat,data=davisdata)
```


## Inferential Tests

```{r}
model1 <- aov(alcohol~Seat,data=davisdata)
summary.aov(model1)
```
The P value 0.000116 is less than 0.05, which means the null hypothesis is failed to reject.Therefore there is a relationship between where a student sits and how much alcohol they drink.

```{r}
plot(TukeyHSD(model1))
```

The tukey graph shows that students in the front back and the middle back tend to show a difference in alcohol consumption. There isn't a difference in alcohol consumption between the front and middle rows.

## Conclusions

The question was if there is a difference between the alcohol consumption between students in the front seat vs. the back seat.
